entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Constantine the Great?
entries.text: Constantine I (27 February 272 – 22 May 337 AD) was a Roman emperor from 306 until he died. He was emperor for longer than any other emperor since Augustus, the first emperor.
entries.title: Constantine the Great

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Mahatma Gandhi?
entries.text: Mohandas Karmchand Gandhi (2 October 1869– 30 January 1948) was a leader of nationalism in British-ruled India. He is more commonly called Mahatma Gandhi. mahatma is an honorific meaning "great-soul" or "venerable" in Sanskrit.
entries.title: Mahatma Gandhi

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Louis Pasteur?
entries.text: Louis Pasteur (December 27, 1822 – September 28, 1895) was a French microbiologist and chemist.
entries.title: Louis Pasteur

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Igor Stravinsky?
entries.text: Igor Stravinsky was born in Lomonosov (then Oranienbaum), 17 June 1882 and died in New York, 6 April 1971. He was one of the most important composers of the 20th century, and a leader in modernism in music.
entries.title: Igor Stravinsky

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Alfred Hitchcock?
entries.text: Sir Alfred Joseph Hitchcock (13 August 1899 – 29 April 1980) was a British movie director who later became an American citizen, but still kept his British citizenship. He mostly made mystery and suspense movies.
entries.title: Alfred Hitchcock

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Conservatism?
entries.text: Conservatism is a type of political belief that supports emphasis on traditions and relies on the individual to maintain society. The term was first used by François-René de Chateaubriand in 1818, during the Bourbon Restoration, which wanted to roll back the policies of the French Revolution.
entries.title: Conservatism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Fascism?
entries.text: Fascism is a far-right form of government where most of the country's power is held by one ruler or a small group, under one political party.
entries.title: Fascism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Time zone?
entries.text: Time zones give specific areas on the Earth a time of day that is earlier or later than the neighboring time zones. This is because when it is daytime on one side of the earth, it is night-time on the other side.
entries.title: Time zone

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Spider?
entries.text: Spiders (class Arachnida, order Araneae) are air-breathing arthropods. They have eight legs, and mouthparts (chelicerae) with fangs that inject venom.
entries.title: Spider

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Sensory system?
entries.text: The sensory system is the way animals find out about their nearby environment and their bodies. To do this they have special devices for collecting data called sense organs.
entries.title: Sensory system

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Disease?
entries.text: A disease or medical condition is an unhealthy state where something bad happens to the body or mind. Diseases can cause pain, parts of the body to stop working the right way, or death.
entries.title: Disease

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Gastroenteritis?
entries.text: Gastroenteritis is a medical term for inflammation of the stomach and intestines. It causes diarrhea, vomiting and stomach pain.
entries.title: Gastroenteritis

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Atom?
entries.text: An atom is an extremely small piece of matter. All normal matter – everything that has mass – is made of atoms.
entries.title: Atom

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Infrared?
entries.text: Infrared (IR) radiation is a type of electromagnetic radiation (a wave with electricity). The wave is longer than light which humans can see and shorter than microwaves.
entries.title: Infrared

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Algebra?
entries.text: Algebra is a part of mathematics. It uses variables to represent a value that is not yet known or can be replaced with any value.
entries.title: Algebra

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Area?
entries.text: Area is the amount of space a two dimensional (flat) surface takes up. It is useful because it is how much of a material is needed to make a hollow container.
entries.title: Area

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Mathematical proof?
entries.text: A mathematical proof is a way to show that a mathematical theorem is true. To prove a theorem is to show that theorem holds in all cases (where it claims to hold).
entries.title: Mathematical proof

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Domestication?
entries.text: Domestication is a change that happens in wild animals or plants, when they are kept by humans for a long time. The Latin term literally means "to make it suitable for home".
entries.title: Domestication

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Juice?
entries.text: Juice is a liquid that comes from plants, animals or fruit. The juice from fruit is often made into a drink.
entries.title: Juice

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Cotton?
entries.text: Cotton is a soft, natural fiber that grows with the seeds of the cotton plant. (Fiber is long and thin, like hair.) After the cotton fiber is gathered from the plant, it can be spun into cotton thread. The cotton thread can then be made into cloth.
entries.title: Cotton

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Plastic?
entries.text: A plastic is a synthetic material that can change its shape easily. Many things are made of plastics, usually because making them to the right shape is easy.
entries.title: Plastic

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is St. Peter's Basilica?
entries.text: St. Peter's Basilica, which is called "Basilica di San Pietro in Vaticano" in Italian, is a large church in Vatican City, an independent country within Rome, Italy. It is often called “the greatest church in Christendom".
entries.title: St. Peter's Basilica

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Animation?
entries.text: Animation is a way of making a movie from many images that don’t move. The images are put together one after another, and then played at a fast speed to make it look like movement.
entries.title: Animation

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Holy Roman Empire?
entries.text: The Holy Roman Empire (Latin: Sacrum Imperium Romanum; German: Heiliges Römisches Reich), occasionally but unofficially referred to as the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation, was a polity in Western and Central Europe under the rule of an emperor, who was elected by the princes and the magistrates of its regions and cities.
entries.title: Holy Roman Empire

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Vikings?
entries.text: The Vikings were Scandinavian people from Northern Europe who were known as great seamen and warriors. The Scandinavian countries include Norway, Sweden and Denmark.
entries.title: Vikings

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Israel?
entries.text: Israel (Hebrew: יִשְׂרָאֵל), officially the State of Israel (Hebrew: מְדִינַת יִשְׂרָאֵל), is a country in southwestern Asia on the eastern side of the Mediterranean Sea. Its capital city is Jerusalem.
entries.title: Israel

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Mexico City?
entries.text: Mexico City is the capital and largest city of Mexico. It's also the most populous city in North America.
entries.title: Mexico City

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Black Sea?
entries.text: The Black Sea is a sea in Eurasia between Europe, Caucasus, and Anatolia. Many important rivers flow to the Black Sea, including the Don, the Danube, the Dniester and the Dnieper.
entries.title: Black Sea

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Volga?
entries.text: The Volga is the longest river in Europe. In Russian it is called Волга, in the Tatar language its name is İdel.
entries.title: Volga

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Andes?
entries.text: The Andes are a mountain range along the western coast of South America.
entries.title: Andes

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Greenland Sea?
entries.text: The Greenland Sea is a body of water. It borders Greenland to the west, the Svalbard archipelago to the east, Fram Strait and the Arctic Ocean to the north, and the Norwegian Sea and Iceland to the south.
entries.title: Greenland Sea

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Aegean Sea?
entries.text: The Aegean Sea, part of the Mediterranean Sea, is between Greece and Anatolia. It is connected in the north to the Sea of Marmara and the Black Sea by the Dardanelles and Bosporus.
entries.title: Aegean Sea

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Timor Sea?
entries.text: The Timor Sea is a relatively shallow sea. It is bounded to the north by the island of Timor, to the east by the Arafura Sea, to the south by Australia and to the west by the Indian Ocean.
entries.title: Timor Sea

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Solomon Sea?
entries.text: The Solomon Sea is a sea in the Pacific Ocean. It is between Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands.
entries.title: Solomon Sea

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Drake Passage?
entries.text: The Drake passage is a body of water. It lies between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
entries.title: Drake Passage

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Aral Sea?
entries.text: The Aral Sea (Kazakh: Арал теңізі (Aral tengizi), Uzbek: Orol dengizi, Russian: Аральскοе мοре) was a lake in Central Asia. It is between Kazakhstan in the north and Karakalpakstan, an autonomous region of Uzbekistan, in the south.
entries.title: Aral Sea

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Spitsbergen?
entries.text: Spitsbergen (which is also spelled Spitzbergen) is the largest island of the archipelago Svalbard. It was called West Spitsbergen until 1965.
entries.title: Spitsbergen

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Yucatán Peninsula?
entries.text: The Yucatán Peninsula is a peninsula in North America. It separates the Caribbean Sea from the Gulf of Mexico.
entries.title: Yucatán Peninsula

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Alborz Mountains?
entries.text: Alborz (also written Alburz, Elburz or Elborz), is a mountain range in northern Iran. Its borders start at Azerbaijan and Armenia in the northwest of Iran and reach to the southern end of the Caspian Sea.
entries.title: Alborz Mountains

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: The Mongolian Plateau or Altai Plateau is a plateau in East Asia. This plateau covers about 3,200,000 square kilometers (1,200,000 sq mi).
entries.title: Mongolian Plateau

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: The Southern Alps is a mountain range in New Zealand. The mountain range runs along the entire length of the South Island.
entries.title: Southern Alps

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: Philadelphia

entries.text: Botswana (officially called the Republic of Botswana) is a country in southern Africa. The capital of Botswana is Gaborone.
entries.title: Botswana

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: A light year (symbol: ly) is the distance that light travels in empty space in one year. entries.text: John Ronald "Johnny" McCormack (August 2, 1925 – February 22, 2017) was a Canadian ice hockey centre. He was born in Edmonton, Alberta. McCormack began his National Hockey League career with the Toronto Maple Leafs in 1947. He also played for the Montreal Canadiens and Chicago Black Hawks. He retired from the NHL in 1955 season. McCormack won two Stanley Cups in his career, one in 1951 with Toronto and another in 1953 with Montreal. He also won the 1945 Memorial Cup with the St. Michael's Majors and the Allan Cup in 1950 with the Toronto Marlboroughs. McCormack died on February 22, 2017 at his home in Oshawa, Ontario, aged 91.
entries.title: John McCormack (ice hockey)
